client_certificate.description:
Reference to a Certificate resource from the certificatemanager.googleapis.com namespace.
Used by a BackendService to negotiate mTLS when the backend connection uses TLS and the backend requests a client certificate. Must have a CLIENT_AUTH scope.
client_certificate.rationale: A reference to another resource (a Certificate Manager certificate). We secure the referenced resource itself, not this pointer to it.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Matches the prevent-destructive-loss archetype: a generic platform policy can require this be set to 'PREVENT' so a security-enforcing backend authentication config cannot be accidentally destroyed via terraform apply/destroy.

description.description: A free-text description of the resource. Max length 1024 characters.
description.rationale: Cosmetic free-text field with no bearing on enforcement.

labels.description:
Set of label tags associated with the BackendAuthenticationConfig resource.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Organisational metadata for filtering/billing; does not affect enforcement.

location.description:
The location of the backend authentication config.
The default value is 'global'.
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

name.rationale: Identifier only; naming has no security bearing.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Identifies which project owns the resource. A generic platform policy cannot constrain this without hardcoding a specific project ID, which is team-specific and out of scope.

trust_config.description:
Reference to a TrustConfig resource from the certificatemanager.googleapis.com namespace.
A BackendService uses the chain of trust represented by this TrustConfig, if specified, to validate the server certificates presented by the backend. Required unless wellKnownRoots is set to PUBLIC_ROOTS.
trust_config.rationale: A reference to another resource (a Certificate Manager TrustConfig). We secure the referenced resource itself, not this pointer to it.

well_known_roots.description:
Well known roots to use for server certificate validation. If set to NONE, the BackendService will only validate server certificates against roots specified in TrustConfig.
If set to PUBLIC_ROOTS, the BackendService uses a set of well-known public roots, in addition to any roots specified in the trustConfig field, when validating the server certificates presented by the backend.
Validation with these roots is only considered when the TlsSettings.sni field in the BackendService is set. The well-known roots are a set of root CAs managed by Google. CAs in this set can be added or removed without notice. Possible values: ["NONE", "PUBLIC_ROOTS"]
well_known_roots.rationale: Controls whether backend server certificate validation trusts Google's externally-managed public root CA set, or only explicit CAs configured in trust_config. Requiring 'NONE' favours explicit, reviewable trust anchors over an externally-controlled root set that can change without notice — consistent with the same trade-off flagged for exclude_public_ca_set on the TLS inspection policy resource.
